title: Frequency-Structured Hamiltonian Neural Network for Multi-Timescale Dynamics
claim: Decompose a signal into frequency-band views, model each with its own component, then aggregate them into one structured predictor.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, three parallel branches fanning out then merging, zoom insets
description: A left-to-right pipeline diagram. At far left is a blue closed, wobbly trajectory plotted on p–q axes, labeled Observed Trajectory. Arrows split it into three horizontal branches colored orange, green and red, for high, medium and low frequency. In each branch a filter icon box leads to a smoothed version of the trajectory (the blue original with a colored overlay that gets coarser from top to bottom). That feeds a labeled box H1, H2 or H3, which produces a multiscale Hamiltonian curve with a dashed zoom-box. The three branches merge into a dashed zoomed inset showing the colored curves. A blue trapezoid labeled M_phi (Hamiltonian Aggregation) then outputs a Predicted Trajectory inset, where a black dashed curve follows the components. The color-coding carries the eye through the figure.
caption: Frequency-Structured Hamiltonian Neural Network. An observed trajectory $z_{\mathrm{train}}$ is filtered into a nested family of low-pass views $z^{(k)}$ at decreasing cutoffs, which expose progressively coarser temporal structure. Each view provides supervision for a per-band Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}^{(k)}_{\theta_{k}}$ that models the dynamics resolved at its cutoff. The aggregator $\mathcal{M}$ combines the per-band Hamiltonians into a single scalar Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{agg}}$, whose canonical dynamics conserve the learned energy and generate the predicted trajectory.
abstract: Learning coupled fast and slow dynamics accurately remains challenging for structure-preserving neural models. Hamiltonian Neural Networks preserve a learned Hamiltonian, but their neural parameterizations are susceptible to spectral bias, which favors slowly varying components and can leave fast oscillations poorly resolved. We introduce the Frequency-Structured Hamiltonian Neural Network (FS-HNN), which organizes Hamiltonian learning across temporal frequency scales. FS-HNN learns Hamiltonian components from frequency-filtered views of observed trajectories and combines them nonlinearly into a single scalar Hamiltonian. This enables the model to represent interactions across timescales while conserving the learned energy in continuous time. For PDEs, FS-HNN represents Hamiltonian components as neural functionals and learns a spatial operator, using orthogonal projection to conserve the learned energy. Experiments on ODE and PDE benchmarks spanning nonlinear oscillators, coupled lattices, shallow water flows, and dispersive waves show that FS-HNN improves long-horizon rollout accuracy over existing baselines, with accompanying gains in physical-energy fidelity.
